newsitem.title: CHINA: China holds German reporter for illegal trip.
newsitem.headline: China holds German reporter for illegal trip.

text.p: Chinese officials have detained a German journalist in the central town of Chaohu, accusing him of visiting the region to carry out reporting activities without permission, the reporter said on Tuesday.
"I was carrying out a private mission," Juergen Kremb, Beijing correspondent for the German magazine Der Spiegel, said by telephone from Chaohu in central Anhui province.

Local police and government authorities detained Kremb and his travelling companion, Wei Xiaotao, brother of jailed dissident Wei Jingsheng, as they were having lunch with several local farmers, relatives of the Wei family, in the town of Bazhen on Monday, he said.
Kremb said he had refused to sign a confession because he had committed no offence.

Local officials had confiscated his passport, Chinese residence permit and plane ticket as well as the ticket of Wei Xiaotao, told the two men to stay in a local hotel and ordered them not to leave the town, Kremb said.
Kremb said he expected the German consulate in Shanghai would send a diplomat to Chaohu to try to sort out the problem.

Kremb said he had long wanted to visit the home town of the family of Wei Jingsheng, regarded as the father of China's beleaguered pro-democracy movement and who is serving the second year of a 14-year jail term for plotting to overthrow the government. Wei was jailed for 15 years from 1979.
Chinese rules prohibit journalists from travelling outside Beijing to carry out reporting activities without permission from the local authorities.

This month, Chinese authorities detained and deported to neighbouring Pakistan a television team from the British Broadcasting Corporation after they were caught working without permission in the restive northwestern region of Xinjiang.
